rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract rather than from measured behaviour. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the body at x = -0.04 to +0.04 m (5 mm steps excluded, 20 mm spacing), placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. Sensor size 0.012 m is smaller than the 25 mm tape, so readings stay sensitive across the tape edge. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn authority. Body 0.12 m wide keeps the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m, a reasonable margin. Mass 0.8 kg is mid-range. Controller: sensor_weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 so the signal is positive when tape is on the left (steer left), matching the sign convention. kp = 2.5 gives a proportional response without saturating the wheels at typical offsets. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. kd = 0.05 adds mild damping against oscillation. base_speed = 1.4 (about 70% of full PWM) is chosen to aim for roughly 1.5 m/s average over 4-5 m, while leaving room to slow for tight bends. line_loss = last_direction so the robot searches toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend with modest oscillation; slalom may be the hardest. The main uncertainties are whether base_speed 1.4 is fast enough to finish within 3 s and whether kp is too low for the tightest bends. Next measurements needed: completion_time and progress (speed adequacy), max_error and steering_oscillation (gain tuning), and line_loss_events (whether the line is lost on sharp bends).
